sq.ANSWER:
Need for Parallel Systems

  • Increasing performance demand: Modern applications like AI, big data analytics, and simulations require processing huge volumes of data quickly.

  • Physical limits of single-core CPUs: Due to heat dissipation and clock speed limits, performance gains now come from parallel execution rather than faster single cores.

  • Energy efficiency: Parallel systems can perform more work per watt compared to pushing a single processor to higher speeds.

  • Real-time processing: Systems like weather forecasting, autonomous driving, and scientific modeling need results in minimal time.

Applications of Parallel Systems

  1. Scientific Simulations – Weather forecasting, climate modeling, astrophysics.

  2. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning – Training deep neural networks.

  3. Big Data Analytics – Processing large datasets in real time.

  4. Engineering Design & Simulation – CAD/CAM, structural analysis, fluid dynamics.

  5. Medical Imaging – MRI, CT scan reconstruction.

  6. Financial Modeling – Stock market prediction, risk analysis.

  7. Multimedia Processing – Real-time rendering, video encoding/decoding.

  8. Cryptography & Security – Large-scale encryption/decryption tasks.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: List the applications and challenges of Parallel systems.

lq.ANSWER:
arallel computing is the process of dividing a large computational problem into smaller tasks that can be executed simultaneously using multiple processors. Instead of relying on a single processor (sequential computing), parallel computing utilizes multiple processors to speed up execution and handle complex problems more efficiently.

Need for Parallel Computing:

  1. Speed and Performance:

    • Sequential execution on a single processor is time-consuming for large-scale problems.

    • Parallel computing reduces execution time by distributing the workload across multiple processors.

    • Example: Weather forecasting simulations that require millions of calculations can be completed faster with parallel systems.

  2. Handling Large Data Sets:

    • Modern applications generate massive amounts of data (big data).

    • Parallel computing allows processing of this data in real-time.

    • Example: Search engines like Google use parallel servers to process queries from millions of users simultaneously.

  3. Solving Complex Problems:

    • Many scientific and engineering problems involve complex mathematical models.

    • These models are often too large for a single processor.

    • Example: Molecular modeling, nuclear simulations, and space exploration rely on parallel processing.

  4. Efficient Resource Utilization:

    • Parallel computing makes use of multi-core processors and distributed systems effectively.

    • It ensures that idle processor cycles are minimized, thus improving resource utilization.

  5. Scalability:

    • Parallel systems can easily scale by adding more processors.

    • This makes them flexible for growing computational demands in research and industries.

  6. Real-Time Processing Needs:

    • Applications like video streaming, online gaming, financial transactions, and air traffic control require instant processing.

    • Parallel computing ensures quick response times by processing multiple tasks concurrently.

Conclusion:
The need for parallel computing arises from the limitations of sequential computing in terms of speed, efficiency, and data handling capacity. With the growth of big data, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and scientific simulations, parallel computing has become an essential approach to meet modern computational demands.
